experiments.name: Long-term archival storage of ice cores at -36 C with sampling in a -24 C examination room (NSF Ice Core Facility)
experiments.plain_name: Keep ice cores frozen in a national archive freezer
experiments.description: Ice cores from Antarctica and Greenland are curated as 1 m sections in tubes on shelves inside a walk-in archive freezer held at -36 C so that trapped gases, chemistry and stratigraphy are preserved; cores are cut and sampled for researchers in an examination room held at -24 C.

requirements.rationale: Archive storage set point -36 C (237.15 K); the storage space must hold this temperature.
requirements.document_title: About - U.S. National Science Foundation Ice Core Facility (NSF-ICF, formerly National Ice Core Laboratory)
requirements.quote: The main archive freezer is ~6,000 square feet (72,000 cubic feet) and is held at a temperature of -36°C.

requirements.rationale: Core examination and sub-sampling are done at -24 C (249.15 K) in a separate room; optional for a storage-only machine.
requirements.document_title: About - U.S. National Science Foundation Ice Core Facility (NSF-ICF, formerly National Ice Core Laboratory)
requirements.quote: The examination room is 1,500 square feet (7,800 cubic feet) and is held at -24°C.

requirements.rationale: Cores are stored as 1 m sections in tubes, so the storage space must accept a 1000 mm long item along its loading/shelf axis (either key satisfies).
requirements.document_title: About - U.S. National Science Foundation Ice Core Facility (NSF-ICF, formerly National Ice Core Laboratory)
requirements.quote: Each silver tube on these shelves contains a 1-meter long section of an ice core.

sources.citation: About - U.S. National Science Foundation Ice Core Facility (NSF-ICF, formerly National Ice Core Laboratory)

experiments.name: Cryogenic vacuum extraction of soil and plant water for d2H/d18O analysis (18-slot manifold, 0.3 Pa, 90 C, liquid-nitrogen U-tube traps)
experiments.plain_name: Pull water out of soil samples under vacuum for isotope tracing
experiments.description: Frozen soil or plant samples in extraction tubes are evacuated to 0.3 Pa, then heated to 90 C in a water bath while the evaporated water is frozen in U-tubes immersed in liquid nitrogen; the recovered water is analysed for stable hydrogen and oxygen isotopes to trace water sources in ecohydrology.

requirements.rationale: The extraction runs under vacuum so water distils from the heated sample to the cold trap.
requirements.document_title: Orlowski N, Frede H-G, Brueggemann N, Breuer L (2013). Validation and application of a cryogenic vacuum extraction system for soil and plant water extraction for isotope analysis. J. Sens. Sens. Syst. 2, 179-193. doi:10.5194/jsss-2-179-2013
requirements.quote: Afterwards, the entire system is evacuated to a pressure of 0.3 Pa.

requirements.rationale: The validated procedure evacuates the line to 0.3 Pa before extraction; the authors note lower pressure may be needed for clay soils.
requirements.document_title: Orlowski N, Frede H-G, Brueggemann N, Breuer L (2013). Validation and application of a cryogenic vacuum extraction system for soil and plant water extraction for isotope analysis. J. Sens. Sens. Syst. 2, 179-193. doi:10.5194/jsss-2-179-2013
requirements.quote: Afterwards, the entire system is evacuated to a pressure of 0.3 Pa.

requirements.rationale: Samples are held at 90 C (363.15 K) for the whole extraction.
requirements.document_title: Orlowski N, Frede H-G, Brueggemann N, Breuer L (2013). Validation and application of a cryogenic vacuum extraction system for soil and plant water extraction for isotope analysis. J. Sens. Sens. Syst. 2, 179-193. doi:10.5194/jsss-2-179-2013
requirements.quote: During the entire extraction process, the samples are heated to 90 °C, leading to the evaporation of water, which is successively trapped in the frozen U-tubes.

requirements.rationale: The evolved vapour is collected in liquid-nitrogen-cooled traps.
requirements.document_title: Orlowski N, Frede H-G, Brueggemann N, Breuer L (2013). Validation and application of a cryogenic vacuum extraction system for soil and plant water extraction for isotope analysis. J. Sens. Sens. Syst. 2, 179-193. doi:10.5194/jsss-2-179-2013
requirements.quote: The sample water evaporates and the evolved vapor is frozen in a cryogenic (liquid nitrogen) trap (Ingraham and Shadel, 1992).

requirements.rationale: Extraction must run to completion to avoid fractionation; the validation runs lasted 180 min.
requirements.document_title: Orlowski N, Frede H-G, Brueggemann N, Breuer L (2013). Validation and application of a cryogenic vacuum extraction system for soil and plant water extraction for isotope analysis. J. Sens. Sens. Syst. 2, 179-193. doi:10.5194/jsss-2-179-2013

experiments.name: In-situ Medusa-GCMS measurement of atmospheric halocarbons, PFCs, SF6 and NMHCs with dual adsorbent traps cooled to -165 C by a Cryotiger
experiments.plain_name: Monitor ozone-depleting and greenhouse gases at a remote air station
experiments.description: Two-litre whole-air samples are preconcentrated on adsorbent micro-traps cooled to -165 C by a closed-cycle Cryotiger cooler, selectively flushed at -70/-125 C to remove CO2, Xe and bulk air, desorbed at +100 C and transferred to a GC-MS, giving 12 air measurements per day of PFCs, SF6, HFCs, HCFCs, CFCs and halons at AGAGE stations.

requirements.rationale: Adsorbent traps must reach -165 C (108.15 K) to retain the most volatile species.

requirements.rationale: Each cycle runs the trap between -165 C trapping and +100 C desorption.

requirements.quote: T1 is heated to 100oC and back-flushed to transfer analytes to T2, held at -165oC.

requirements.rationale: Preconcentrated analytes are separated and detected by the coupled GC-MS.

experiments.name: Homogeneous freezing of supercooled H2SO4/H2O aerosol by expansion cooling in the 84 m3 AIDA chamber (189-235 K)
experiments.plain_name: Make artificial cirrus clouds from acid droplets in a giant chamber
experiments.description: Submicron sulphuric acid droplets are added to the evacuated, re-filled and ice-coated 84 m3 AIDA vessel at 189-235 K; pumping expansions cool the gas at up to 2.8 K/min until the droplets freeze, detected by laser depolarisation, optical counters and hygrometers, to derive ice-nucleation thresholds for upper-tropospheric cirrus.

requirements.rationale: The freezing experiments spanned 189-235 K.
requirements.document_title: Moehler O, Stetzer O, Schaefers S, et al. (2003). Experimental investigation of homogeneous freezing of sulphuric acid particles in the aerosol chamber AIDA. Atmos. Chem. Phys. 3, 211-223. doi:10.5194/acp-3-211-2003
requirements.quote: 24 freezing experiments were performed at temperatures between 189 and 235 K with aerosol particles in the diameter range 0.05 to 1 µm.

requirements.rationale: The vessel is evacuated and flushed before each series and pumped to expand-cool the gas.

experiments.name: Heterogeneous ice nucleation on Asian and Saharan desert dust during AIDA expansion runs from -20 C to -65 C

notes: Ten environmental-science profiles, each requirement quoted from a fetched source (accessed 2026-11-01). Tavily, Lune and WebSearch quotas were exhausted during this run, so sources are limited to idea URLs plus pages/papers reachable by direct WebFetch; quotes from PDFs were taken from pdftotext extraction (degree signs restored as printed, e.g. -34 °C). Not covered: TO-15 canister VOCs (duplicates existing expansion_b_env_whole_air_voc_cryofocusing) and the Radiocarbon sediment-DIC distillation (source URL redirects to journal home page). The Medusa Bristol page quotes 'Cryotiger' but does not state cryogen-free operation, so no cryogen.cryogen_free requirement was written. AIDA chamber.volume >= 84 m3 is mandatory because the published cloud-expansion method relies on the large vessel; only cloud-simulation chambers of that size can pass. HPGe temperature.base <= 77 K follows the NRA manual; electrically cooled detectors documented warmer than 77 K would fail it. Specimen-bank profile uses the German ESB specimen-archive page (with NIST Biorepository as corroborating source).
